title: Fold a lever nail clipper shut for storage
instruction: Fold the nail clipper shut for storage: its lever is raised for cutting and must end folded flat along the upper blade, pointing to the tail. Leave the clipper in the tray slot and move both grippers clear.
context: Societal relatability: a lever nail clipper is in most homes, and nearly everyone has opened one to cut and folded it shut again so that it drops into a drawer, bag or pocket without snagging. The fold is not a press: pushed down, the lever only bears on its heel. The lever is held on two axes at once. The pin swivels in the blades and the lever hinges on the pin, so it has to be swung half a turn and turned over. On a 54 g part that slides and tips easily, that is a small, exact two-step motion.
setup: A grooming tray is fixed to the table in front of the right arm: a slot 88 x 18 mm and 7 mm deep, its long side pointing away from the robot. A steel lever nail clipper, 85 mm long, 15 mm wide, 54 g, lies loose in the slot (1.5 mm of play each way), jaws toward the robot. Lower blade: 85 x 15 x 2 mm, flat on the slot floor. Upper blade: 2 mm thick, riveted to the lower one at the tail, rising 5.5 degrees from the tail and level over its last 22 mm, where the two cutting edges stand 2.4 mm apart. A 3.5 mm pin stands 14 mm behind the cutting edges. It passes through a hole in the upper blade and swivels freely in the lower one. The lever (57 mm from hinge to tip, 12 mm wide, 2.2 mm thick, 10 g) hinges on the pin 12.5 mm above the slot floor. A heel 3.5 mm high, 6 mm from the hinge, stands on the level part of the upper blade, so the lever starts raised about 19 degrees, pointing to the tail, its tip 31 mm above the floor: the cutting position. The heel stands on that level part at every swing angle, so the lever's lower stop is the same all the way round. Folded, the lever points to the tail again but turned over: heel side up, its tip on the upper blade, 6 degrees below level (its upper stop). Two routes get there. Swing the raised lever half a turn about the pin (it then points out past the jaws, 19 degrees up) and flip it over the top; or flip it over first (it then lies pointing out past the jaws, heel side up, on the jaw end) and swing it half a turn. Either way round the pin works. Nothing latches: the lever stays where gravity and the blade leave it. Both grippers start open, at least 150 mm from the clipper. Run limit 800 steps (40 s).
scoring: Read at the end of the run; nothing is latched. Plan directions are taken along the lower blade, from the pin. 1.0: the lever points to the tail within 10 degrees in plan, heel side up, the underside of its tip no more than 2 mm above the upper blade (feeler gauge); the clipper lies in the slot with all four corners of the lower blade within 1.5 mm of the slot floor; the fingers of each gripper are 30 mm or more from every part of the clipper; and for the last second (20 steps) all of this held and neither the lever's tip nor the two ends of the lower blade moved more than 1 mm. 0.5: the lever points to the tail within 10 degrees in plan with its heel side facing away from the lower blade (over the top, but not flat, not clear or not still). 0.25: the lever points out past the jaws, within 30 degrees of the blade's line in plan, either way up (half of the fold, by either route). 0: anything else. The start scores 0: the lever points to the tail heel side down. So does pressing the lever down and holding it there.
fidelity: Size and mass are those of large lever nail clippers on sale (82 to 92 mm, 45 to 60 g). Blades and lever are flat plates and the cutting edges square lips, not ground. The two blades are one rigid part: pushed down, the lever bears on its heel and the jaws do not close (a real pair close 2.4 mm and spring back). The lever's two rests on the blade are stops in its hinge, set where heel and tip meet the blade. The pin turns in place. Nothing is latched or moved by code.
reset_notes: Put the clipper in the slot, jaws toward the robot. Turn the lever to the cutting position: pointing to the tail, heel down on the upper blade, raised about 20 degrees. Check that the jaws stand open and that the lever swivels freely. Open both grippers and park them 150 mm or more from the clipper.
